sections.title: Quick answer

body: The four INFJ letters stand for Introversion, Intuition, Feeling and Judging in the Myers–Briggs framework. This page uses Ni–Fe–Ti–Se to explain MBTI type dynamics. NERIS uses its own framework and adds Identity to its INFJ code. The suffix changes neither those four letters nor the MBTI function notation.

In a fictional example, two speakers give the same forty-minute talk from the same script and receive the same feedback: part of the talk made someone uncomfortable. Both ask which part, review the same passage and check the source of the same figure.

After making the same correction, someone closer to A might still feel confident about the rest of the talk. Someone closer to T might feel less sure about the talk as a whole. Either feeling can occur in the same person on another occasion.
The NERIS definition does not set a recovery-time threshold. For reflection, notice how sure you felt before you asked for clarification and how you felt after getting it.

For the four preferences and their function notation, read the [INFJ profile](/en/personality/infj). For A and T, see the [NERIS framework](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory). The F in INFJ stands for Feeling. The letter after the hyphen describes Identity.
sections.title: INFJ-A and INFJ-T: what they share and where they part

body: The table compares internal reactions in fictional examples. In each row both speakers have the same information, responsibilities and deadline.
If one person gave the talk and the other only helped prepare it, their reactions could reflect the difference in responsibility. The table keeps those conditions the same.
Neither column predicts what a person will do or how well they did. The shared-action column shows actions anyone could take.

| Same situation | Shared action | Assertive (A): possible self-evaluation | Turbulent (T): possible self-evaluation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hearing the same feedback | Ask which part concerned the participant | May still feel confident in the rest of the talk | May feel less sure about the rest of the talk |
| After receiving the same clarification | Check the relevant passage and add the source | May feel confident in the remaining explanation | May still wonder whether the rest of the explanation is adequate |
| The participant pauses for an unknown reason | Ask whether they want to add anything | May still feel the talk was broadly clear | May feel less certain that the talk was clear |
| After the same omission is reported to the organiser | Explain the omission and supply the same material | May still feel their overall assessment of the talk holds | May feel less confident in their overall assessment of the talk |
| After confirming the same follow-up | Record what was agreed | May feel sure they handled the concern adequately | May still worry they did not explain it clearly |
| After reviewing the same late change of topic | Compare the same prepared sections with the new brief | May still feel confident in their judgment of what will work | May feel less sure about their judgment of what will work |
An incorrect fact calls for a source check regardless of how confident either speaker feels. If the issue is pace, either can repeat the explanation more slowly.
sections.title: INFJ-A and INFJ-T in one minute

body: These fictional scenarios hold the task and responsibilities constant and compare how the speakers might feel after doing the same work.
### INFJ-A and INFJ-T facing the same challenge
(Fictional example) Two speakers give the same community talk, from the same script, with the same room deadline. Each hears the same concern from a participant.

Both check the same passage, add the same source and agree on follow-up. After that correction, one speaker might feel sure the rest of the talk stands. Another might feel less confident about the rest of it. That difference illustrates self-evaluation and can vary from one occasion to the next.
### INFJ-A and INFJ-T at work or study: a late change of topic
(Fictional example) Three days before a talk, the organiser changes the brief from reading strategies to an introduction to writing. Both speakers have the same materials and preparation time.

Both check the same brief and review the same three sections. Someone closer to Assertive might still feel confident about their assessment of the revised talk. Someone closer to Turbulent might feel less certain about that same assessment. Both can make the same revisions.

Mark which sections still fit the brief and which need rewriting. Assign the work by responsibility, available time and subject knowledge. How confident someone feels does not establish whether their plan will work.
sections.title: INFJ-A and INFJ-T: feedback and a change of topic

body: A/T describes self-assurance and responses to pressure within NERIS. It is not a resilience score or a measure of judgment accuracy.

Use the script, the participant’s words and the corrected source to check what happened. Record how it felt separately. The record of the work and the person’s own evaluation answer different questions.
The hyphen marks a separate NERIS dimension. INFJ still has N in the second position and F in the third. Shared codes across instruments do not establish that the scoring is the same.
Repeatedly checking a source can reflect the job, a deadline or a verification requirement. It cannot establish an A/T result.
sections.title: INFJ-A and INFJ-T: avoiding misreads

body: Use this exercise to understand how a particular situation felt. It is for reflection and cannot establish an A/T result or guide job selection.
Record what was corrected, what the task required and how confident you felt afterwards. Keep those notes separate so you can see the difference between correcting the work and evaluating yourself.

After feedback, write how sure you felt about your original judgment and how much pressure you felt. Revisit those two notes after clarification. You can use words or an informal scale to track changes. There is no cutoff or result to calculate.
Stop if keeping the notes makes you dwell on the incident or interferes with sleep or work. If sleep problems or low mood persist, consider seeking qualified support.

body: **Framework sources.** The definitions of the two ends follow the [NERIS explanation from 16Personalities](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) and the [dedicated Identity page](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent); the four-letter part refers to the [Foundation's type dynamics table](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

**Function-stack convention.** This page uses Ni–Fe–Ti–Se for INFJ in MBTI type dynamics. The Foundation’s overview also allows Te in the tertiary position. NERIS Identity does not change this notation or establish a person’s behaviour, competence or compatibility.
**Editorial fiction.** The talk feedback, revised brief and observation exercise illustrate self-evaluation. They do not measure any individual or establish how often a reaction occurs.

**Scope.** Form M reports four-letter MBTI distributions and cannot establish the proportion at either end of NERIS Identity. The suffix is unsuitable for hiring, ranking ability or predicting relationships. FermatMind uses its own questions and scoring. See the [method and evidence statement](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).

body: These fictional scenarios hold the task and responsibilities constant and compare how the speakers might feel after doing the same work.
### INFJ-A and INFJ-T facing the same challenge
(Fictional example) Two speakers give the same community talk, from the same script, with the same room deadline. Each hears the same concern from a participant.

Both check the same passage, add the same source and agree on follow-up. After that correction, one speaker might feel sure the rest of the talk stands. Another might feel less confident about the rest of it. That difference illustrates self-evaluation and can vary from one occasion to the next.
### INFJ-A and INFJ-T at work or study: a late change of topic
(Fictional example) Three days before a talk, the organiser changes the brief from reading strategies to an introduction to writing. Both speakers have the same materials and preparation time.

Both check the same brief and review the same three sections. Someone closer to Assertive might still feel confident about their assessment of the revised talk. Someone closer to Turbulent might feel less certain about that same assessment. Both can make the same revisions.

Mark which sections still fit the brief and which need rewriting. Assign the work by responsibility, available time and subject knowledge. How confident someone feels does not establish whether their plan will work.

body: A/T describes self-assurance and responses to pressure within NERIS. It is not a resilience score or a measure of judgment accuracy.

Use the script, the participant’s words and the corrected source to check what happened. Record how it felt separately. The record of the work and the person’s own evaluation answer different questions.
The hyphen marks a separate NERIS dimension. INFJ still has N in the second position and F in the third. Shared codes across instruments do not establish that the scoring is the same.
Repeatedly checking a source can reflect the job, a deadline or a verification requirement. It cannot establish an A/T result.
sections.title: INFJ-A and INFJ-T: avoiding misreads

body: Use this exercise to understand how a particular situation felt. It is for reflection and cannot establish an A/T result or guide job selection.
Record what was corrected, what the task required and how confident you felt afterwards. Keep those notes separate so you can see the difference between correcting the work and evaluating yourself.

After feedback, write how sure you felt about your original judgment and how much pressure you felt. Revisit those two notes after clarification. You can use words or an informal scale to track changes. There is no cutoff or result to calculate.
Stop if keeping the notes makes you dwell on the incident or interferes with sleep or work. If sleep problems or low mood persist, consider seeking qualified support.

body: **Framework sources.** The definitions of the two ends follow the [NERIS explanation from 16Personalities](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) and the [dedicated Identity page](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent); the four-letter part refers to the [Foundation's type dynamics table](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

**Function-stack convention.** This page uses Ni–Fe–Ti–Se for INFJ in MBTI type dynamics. The Foundation’s overview also allows Te in the tertiary position. NERIS Identity does not change this notation or establish a person’s behaviour, competence or compatibility.
**Editorial fiction.** The talk feedback, revised brief and observation exercise illustrate self-evaluation. They do not measure any individual or establish how often a reaction occurs.

**Scope.** Form M reports four-letter MBTI distributions and cannot establish the proportion at either end of NERIS Identity. The suffix is unsuitable for hiring, ranking ability or predicting relationships. FermatMind uses its own questions and scoring. See the [method and evidence statement](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).

sections.body_md:
**Framework sources.** The definitions of the two ends follow the [NERIS explanation from 16Personalities](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) and the [dedicated Identity page](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent); the four-letter part refers to the [Foundation's type dynamics table](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

**Function-stack convention.** This page uses Ni–Fe–Ti–Se for INFJ in MBTI type dynamics. The Foundation’s overview also allows Te in the tertiary position. NERIS Identity does not change this notation or establish a person’s behaviour, competence or compatibility.

**Editorial fiction.** The talk feedback, revised brief and observation exercise illustrate self-evaluation. They do not measure any individual or establish how often a reaction occurs.

**Scope.** Form M reports four-letter MBTI distributions and cannot establish the proportion at either end of NERIS Identity. The suffix is unsuitable for hiring, ranking ability or predicting relationships. FermatMind uses its own questions and scoring. See the [method and evidence statement](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).
